title: Start the disk alarm from a complete object

blocks.text: The ops team watches disk usage through a monitoring feed. A `DiskAlarm` raises an alarm for each reading of its volume at or above its limit. The feed sends a new listener the latest reading of every volume as soon as it subscribes, so an alarm started while a disk is already at 97 % should raise at once.

Two complaints came in about the old version: an alarm started on a full disk stayed silent until the next reading, and an alarm whose limit was typed as `0` was refused with an error, yet the feed's listener count kept growing with every such attempt.

Finish the private constructor and `watch(...)` in `src/main/java/practice/DiskAlarm.java`. When you're done, `watch` either returns an alarm that hears every reading from the latest ones on, or throws `IllegalArgumentException` for a limit outside 1 to 99 and leaves the feed as it was. About six lines in total.

cases.says: an alarm raises once per reading of its own volume at or above its limit, and ignores other volumes
the latest reading the feed sends a new listener is judged with the alarm's real volume and limit
a watch refused for its limit leaves no listener on the feed

origin.section: A Constructor That Hands Out this Lets Others Use a Half-Built Object

concepts: An object that hands out this from its constructor can be called before its fields are assigned, final ones included, and stays referenced even when the constructor then throws.
A private constructor that validates and assigns, with a static factory that publishes the finished object, keeps half-built and refused objects out of other code.
